subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Prophet (S.A.W.)’s Journey to Taif
overview: After years of calling the people of Makkah, the Prophet (S.A.W) travelled to Taif to invite its people to Islam. They rejected him and treated him harshly. In this sub-strand you will narrate that journey and learn the patience, tolerance and perseverance he showed.

lessons.title: Why the Prophet went to Taif
objectives: Explain why the Prophet (S.A.W) travelled to Taif.
Narrate how the leaders and the people responded.
lessons.intro: A caller does not stop because the first town refuses. About ten years after prophethood, with his protectors in Makkah gone, the Prophet (S.A.W) walked to Taif to offer the same message.
lessons.notes:
### Why he went
For years the Prophet (S.A.W) had called the people of Makkah to worship Allah alone. Many of them insulted him and harmed his followers. Then his uncle Abu Talib, who had protected him, died, and his wife Khadijah (R.A.) also died. That time is remembered as a year of grief. With less protection in Makkah, he looked for another people who might accept Islam and give the Muslims support.

Taif is a town near Makkah. Its people were called Thaqif. The Prophet (S.A.W) went there and spoke to their leaders, among them Ibn Abd Yalil. He invited them to Islam and asked for their help.

### How they treated him
The leaders refused. They did not respond as he had hoped. The people mocked him and set youths and others to shout at him and throw stones until he was injured and his feet bled. He left Taif deeply grieved. This was not a small disagreement. It was cruelty towards a man who had come with a peaceful call.

He later told Aisha (R.A.) that the day of Taif was harder for him than the day of Uhud (Bukhari). That comparison, from his own words, shows how heavy the rejection was.

### What to remember in the story
He did not go to Taif to fight or to seize property. He went to invite people to Allah. Their answer was insults and stones. The next lessons look at what he did with that pain. For this lesson, be able to retell the reason for the journey and the way the people of Taif treated him, in the correct order, without adding events you are not sure of.

keyWords.meaning: a town near Makkah whose people the Prophet (S.A.W) invited to Islam
the time when Abu Talib and Khadijah (R.A.) died, before the journey to Taif

examples.problem: A learner says the Prophet (S.A.W) went to Taif to punish the people. What is the correct reason?
steps: He had lost protection in Makkah after the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah.
He went to invite the people to Islam and to seek support.
examples.answer: He went to call them to Allah, not to punish them.

activity.title: Listen and retell the journey
materials: A story of the journey to Taif from a resource person, course book or digital device
steps: Listen to or watch the story of the Prophet's journey to Taif.
Each learner retells it individually to the class or to a partner, in order: why he went, whom he met, and how they treated him.
The class adds any important point that was missed, without inventing new events.
Write the retelling in five sentences in your notebook.

practice.question: Why did the Prophet (S.A.W) travel to Taif?
practice.answer: To invite the people to Islam and to seek support after he had less protection in Makkah.

practice.question: Which two deaths made this period a year of grief?
practice.answer: The deaths of his uncle Abu Talib and his wife Khadijah (R.A.).

practice.question: How did the people of Taif treat him?
practice.answer: They rejected his call, mocked him and threw stones at him until he was injured.

practice.question: Which day did the Prophet (S.A.W) say was harder than the day of Uhud?
practice.answer: The day of his rejection at Taif.

summary: The Prophet (S.A.W) went to Taif to call its people to Islam after a time of grief in Makkah.
The people mocked him and stoned him until he was injured.

lessons.title: His dua, and how he treated the people of Taif
objectives: Narrate what the Prophet (S.A.W) did after he left the town.
Explain how he treated the people who had harmed him.
lessons.intro: Anyone who has been chased and injured might want revenge. The Prophet (S.A.W) turned to Allah, accepted kindness from a servant, and refused to ask for the town to be destroyed.
lessons.notes:
### Rest and dua
In the account of the journey, the Prophet (S.A.W) took rest in a garden outside Taif. The garden belonged to two men of Makkah, Utbah and Shaybah. He turned to Allah and complained of his weakness, of having little support, and of being looked down on by people. He asked Allah for mercy. He made it clear that as long as Allah was not displeased with him, he could bear the hardship. That dua shows trust. He took his pain to Allah before he thought of punishing people.

The owners of the garden felt sorry for him and sent their servant Addas with grapes. Addas was a Christian from Nineveh. When the Prophet said Bismillah before eating, Addas was surprised, because that was not the custom of the people around them. The Prophet told him about Yunus (A.S.), who was also from Nineveh. Addas recognised the truth and honoured him. One servant believed, even though the leaders had refused.

### The angel of the mountains
Aisha (R.A.) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari that as the Prophet (S.A.W) left, grieving, Angel Jibril (A.S.) came and said that Allah had heard what the people had said. The angel of the mountains was present and offered to crush the people of Taif between the two mountains if the Prophet wished.

The Prophet (S.A.W) said no. He hoped that Allah would bring from their children people who would worship Allah alone, without partners.

### How he treated them
He did not curse them with destruction. He did not ask for revenge. He chose patience and mercy, and he kept a hope for guidance. That is the answer to the question, "How did the Prophet treat the people of Taif?" He treated them with forgiveness and with dua for a better future, after they had treated him with stones.

keyWords.meaning: the servant in the garden who brought grapes and honoured the Prophet (S.A.W)
bearing hurt without rushing to revenge
continuing a good aim even when it is very hard

examples.problem: The angel of the mountains offered to crush Taif. What did the Prophet (S.A.W) choose, and what hope did he give as his reason?
steps: He hoped their descendants would worship Allah alone.
examples.answer: He said no. He hoped Allah would bring from their children people who would worship Allah alone.

activity.title: Virtues on a chart
steps: Retell the second part of the story: the garden, the dua, Addas, and the angel of the mountains.
Identify the virtues in the story, especially patience, tolerance and perseverance, and write each one on a chart with one sentence from the journey.
A learner explains how the Prophet treated the people of Taif.

practice.question: What did the Prophet (S.A.W) do with his pain before any talk of punishment?
practice.answer: He turned to Allah in dua and complained of his weakness, asking for Allah's mercy.

practice.question: Who was Addas, and what did he bring?
practice.answer: He was a servant in the garden, from Nineveh. He brought grapes.

practice.question: What offer did the angel of the mountains make?
practice.answer: He offered to crush the people of Taif between the two mountains.

practice.question: How did the Prophet (S.A.W) treat the people of Taif?
practice.answer: He forgave them in the sense that he refused revenge and hoped their children would worship Allah alone.

summary: The Prophet (S.A.W) made dua and accepted kindness from Addas.
He refused the offer to destroy Taif.
He hoped that later generations would worship Allah alone.

lessons.title: Patience, tolerance and perseverance
objectives: Show what patience, tolerance and perseverance looked like on the journey to Taif.
Name situations in a learner's life that need the same virtues.
lessons.intro: The journey to Taif is not only a story to remember. It is a pattern for hard days: do not answer cruelty with cruelty, and do not abandon a good aim because people refuse it.
lessons.notes:
### The three virtues
- Patience (sabr): he bore insults, stones and grief without giving up his manners. Patience is staying calm and obedient to Allah when something hurts.
- Tolerance: he allowed the people time and refused revenge. Tolerance does not mean calling a wrong thing right. Their treatment was wrong. Tolerance means he did not repay wrong with a worse wrong.
- Perseverance: he had already called Makkah for years, and after Taif he continued the mission. Perseverance is staying on a good path after failure and pain.

He also showed mercy, trust in Allah, and hope. Those virtues sit inside the three named for this sub-strand.

### Where learners need them
- Patience: when you are ill, when a parent corrects you, when homework is difficult, or when you must wait your turn.
- Tolerance: when a classmate mocks your hijab, your name or your prayer. You do not hit back or insult their family. You report bullying to a teacher, and you keep your dignity.
- Perseverance: when you fail a recitation and must repeat it, when friends tell you to stop trying, or when a good habit is hard to keep for a whole month.

### What these virtues are not
Patience is not silence in the face of danger. A child who is being harmed tells a trusted adult. The Prophet (S.A.W) left Taif; he did not stay to be stoned again that day. He was patient, and he also moved to safety. Tolerance is not joining wrongdoing to please people. Perseverance is not repeating a careless mistake; it is continuing the right effort in a better way.

Appreciating the virtues means you admire them in him and you practise a small piece of them this week.

keyWords.meaning: hurting or mocking someone again and again

examples.problem: A boy knocks Yusuf's books down and laughs. Yusuf wants to throw a stone. Which virtue from Taif should he use, and what should he actually do?
steps: Throwing a stone copies the people of Taif, not the Prophet.
Tolerance and patience mean he does not take revenge. He should also get help if the bullying continues.
examples.answer: He should not throw anything. He should stay calm, pick up his books, and tell a teacher if it happens again.

activity.title: When we need these virtues
materials: The class chart of virtues from the journey
steps: In groups, brainstorm situations at home and at school that need patience, situations that need tolerance, and situations that need perseverance.
Present one situation for each virtue, and say what a Muslim learner should do.
Discuss the difference between patience and keeping silent when you are in danger.
Each learner writes one virtue to practise this week and the situation in which he or she will use it.

practice.question: Give one action on the journey to Taif that shows patience.
practice.answer: He bore insults and stones without replying with cruelty, and he turned to dua.

practice.question: How did he show tolerance towards the people of Taif?
practice.answer: He refused the offer to destroy them and hoped their children would become believers.

practice.question: What is perseverance, using the journey as your example?
practice.answer: Continuing the call to Allah after rejection and pain, instead of abandoning the mission.

practice.question: A classmate mocks you for praying. What should you do, and what should you not do?
practice.answer: Stay calm, continue the prayer, and tell a teacher if it continues. Do not insult or hit back.

summary: Patience, tolerance and perseverance are the virtues of the journey to Taif.
He refused revenge and continued the mission.
Learners practise the same virtues at home and at school, and still report real harm.

quiz.question: Why did the Prophet (S.A.W) go to Taif?
options: invite the people to Islam and seek support
quiz.explanation: The journey was a call to Allah after he had less protection in Makkah.

quiz.question: The year of grief is linked to the deaths of which people?
quiz.explanation: His uncle and his wife died, and protection in Makkah grew weaker.

quiz.question: How did the people of Taif respond to his call?
options: They rejected him, mocked him and threw stones
They walked with him to Madinah that same day
quiz.explanation: The call was refused and he was injured.

quiz.question: He described the day of Taif as harder than which of these?
options: a journey to the cave only
quiz.explanation: This is reported from him in Sahih al-Bukhari.

quiz.question: After the stoning he turned first to…
quiz.explanation: He complained of his weakness to Allah and asked for mercy.

quiz.question: Addas is remembered because…
quiz.answer: He was the servant who brought grapes, heard the name of Allah, and honoured the Prophet.
quiz.explanation: A servant responded with respect when the leaders had refused.

quiz.question: When the angel of the mountains offered to crush Taif, what did the Prophet (S.A.W) do?
options: refused and hoped their children would worship Allah alone
quiz.explanation: His choice is the clearest lesson of mercy from the journey.

quiz.question: Which virtue is shown by refusing revenge?
quiz.explanation: Tolerance here means bearing the wrong without repaying it with destruction.

quiz.question: Perseverance on this journey means…
options: continuing the mission after pain and rejection
quiz.explanation: He did not abandon the call because Taif refused him.

quiz.question: A learner teased for praying should…
options: stay calm, keep praying, and tell a teacher if the teasing continues
quiz.explanation: This copies his patience and still uses a safe way to stop bullying.

quiz.question: Why do Muslims appreciate the virtues he showed in Taif?
quiz.answer: Because he answered cruelty with patience, mercy and hope, and those qualities guide Muslims in their own hard times.
quiz.explanation: Appreciation means admiring the virtues and trying to practise them.
